title: hotfix(slo-enforcer): smooth regional backoff thresholds to avoid thrashing and over-shedding
author: Connor Li
description: Fixes a regression in the SLO enforcer where rapid oscillation in regional latency signals caused aggressive circuit-breaker tripping and cross-region failovers. This resulted in customer-facing tail latency spikes and repeated capacity churn during transient infra noise. The change introduces: 1) exponential smoothing on per-region SLO windows, 2) a minimum open/closed hysteresis interval to prevent immediate reopen/reclose within short windows, 3) a corrected backoff computation when multiple tiers are attached, and 4) additional metrics and dashboards to detect overshedding. Includes unit and integration tests, config migration for existing clusters, and a short rollback plan. Linear: ENG-8123, SRE-234.

release_notes: Hotfix: Reduce SLO enforcer overshedding in regional failover scenarios by adding EWMA smoothing and hysteresis. Customers should see fewer cross-region failovers during short-lived infra noise. No config change required for default deployments; operators can tune 'slo_enforcer.ewma_alpha' and 'slo_enforcer.hysteresis_ms' for aggressive workloads.
risk_and_mitigation: Low-medium. Changes are localized to the SLO enforcer and accompanied by a rollout plan: gradual canary (10% regions) -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback on elevated shedding metric. Added metric 'slo_enforcer.overshed.rate' and an alert to revert if it increases beyond threshold.
rollback_plan: Revert config flag 'slo_enforcer.enable_ewma' or deploy previous release build. Runbook documented at docs/runbooks/slo-enforcer-overshed.md.
notes_for_release_manager: Deploy during low-traffic window; watch slo_enforcer.overshed.rate and region_failover.count for 60m post-deploy. Contact SRE on-call if alert fires.
human_readable_summary: This PR fixes a regression where rapid oscillation in regional latency signals caused the SLO enforcer to thrash tripping circuit-breakers and triggering unnecessary cross-region failovers. The fix smooths signals and prevents immediate reopen/reclose cycles, reducing customer-side latency spikes and capacity churn.
